Container.Name: NNTmux
Container.Overview:
NNTmux Usenet indexer in a single container. Bundles MariaDB, Redis and Manticore plus the web UI, queue workers, scheduler and the tmux indexing engine.
First run creates the database and admin user from the variables below, so fill in the NNTP and Admin settings before starting. Config, database and search data live in /config. NZBs and covers live in /data.
Container.Requires: Usenet provider account (NNTP). First run needs ADMIN_USER, ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASS (12+ chars) and the NNTP settings.
Container.Changes:
### 2026-10-09 - Compressed headers no longer fail to download (they were often cut off), and part repair works again
### 2026-10-08 - PreDB matching works again when releases are created (it failed on every lookup) - Faster article decoding (native yEnc decoder) - Compressed headers from your Usenet provider, on by default
### 2026-10-06 - Latest NNTmux: new settings system, faster PreDB matching - Database updates now run automatically when the container updates - tmux 3.7b and a UTF-8 locale (fixes the indexer not starting) - Fixed groups getting stuck re-reading years-old posts - Fixed password-protected releases being offered to Sonarr/Radarr - Removes fake releases that only contain PAR2 repair files
### 2026-10-04 - Much faster release processing with a full PreDB (added a missing database index) - Far fewer database lock errors under heavy load - Headers that hit a lock are retried longer and repaired later instead of lost
### 2026-10-02 - New: IRC PRE scraper nick, Look inside releases, Use PAR2 names, Fix release names, Pulse monitoring, Minimum release size (MB) - Latest NNTmux, including security fixes - Faster database settings, system security updates - Sharper icon
### 2026-09-22 - Initial release

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: Web interface port

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Settings, database, Redis and Manticore data

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: NZB files and cover images. Grows large, put it on the array if you like.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User id the services run as

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group id the services run as

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone, for example America/Chicago

Config.Name: Site URL
Config.Description: URL you will use to reach the site, including port

Config.Name: NNTP Server
Config.Description: Usenet provider hostname

Config.Name: NNTP Port
Config.Description: 563 for SSL, 119 for plain

Config.Name: NNTP SSL
Config.Description: true or false

Config.Name: NNTP Connections
Config.Description: Connections your provider allows

Config.Name: Admin Username
Config.Description: Created on first run

Config.Name: Admin Password
Config.Description: At least 12 characters. Used on first run only.

Config.Name: Admin Email
Config.Description: Created on first run

Config.Name: IRC PRE scraper nick
Config.Description: Nick for the PRE scraper (#PreNNTmux on SynIRC). Must be unique, add a few random characters, e.g. yourname_k7q2x. Setting a nick turns the scraper on.

Config.Name: Look inside releases
Config.Description: Reads file lists inside releases so hashed names can be renamed

Config.Name: Use PAR2 names
Config.Description: Uses PAR2 file names to rename releases

Config.Name: Fix release names
Config.Description: Renames releases using NFOs, PAR2 and file names (same as Admin, Tmux, Fix Release Names)

Config.Name: Pulse monitoring
Config.Description: Laravel Pulse. Grows the database fast, leave off unless you need it

Config.Name: Minimum release size (MB)
Config.Description: Skip releases smaller than this. Stops broken one-file fragments of obfuscated posts from cluttering the index.

Config.Name: Compressed headers
Config.Description: Ask your Usenet provider for compressed headers (much less bandwidth). Set to false if your provider does not support XFEATURE COMPRESS GZIP.

Config.Name: Start indexer
Config.Description: Set false to run only the web UI without the tmux indexing engine

Config.Name: MariaDB buffer pool
Config.Description: MariaDB memory cache. Set to about half your spare RAM (e.g. 8G, 16G, 32G). Bigger is faster.
